lines.text: ready = deque(j for j in jobs if indeg[j] == 0)
return order  # jobs left with indeg > 0 are silently dropped
if len(order) < len(jobs): raise CycleError(sorted(set(jobs) - set(order)))

sources.cite: ACM/IEEE-CS/AAAI, Computer Science Curricula 2023 (CS2023), knowledge areas (AL: Algorithmic Foundations)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the report's first part: AL, Algorithmic Foundations, is one of 17 knowledge areas; the fetch did not reach its topic lists. The MSCS course cites CS2023 and MIT 6.006 for its graph units (dated 2026-11-11, not re-read).

Larkhill Freight, its jobs and times are invented teaching values. The planner is Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly take a node with in-degree 0; a directed graph has a topological order exactly when this removes every node, so nodes left over lie on or behind a cycle. That is the standard result, stated here as the author's; no page carrying it was opened for this round.

brief.situation: You look after the nightly analytics pipeline at Larkhill Freight (fictional). A planner orders the 12 jobs in jobs.yaml so each runs after the jobs it depends on. Last night's run reported success, but the morning reports are missing three tables. Yesterday two dependencies were added. The rerun window closes at 05:40. It is 04:50.
handover: reports_cache is meant to be built from reports, to speed up the dashboard.
finance_close needs the ledger load; it should not need reports.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: inspect the plan or the graph, change jobs.yaml or the planner, run a check, or rerun the pipeline. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Rerunning is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the team: why three jobs never ran, what you changed, and how you know the order is right.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Kahn's topological sort only places jobs whose dependencies are all placed; yesterday's edges made a cycle (reports -> finance_close -> reports_cache -> reports), so those three never reached in-degree 0, and the planner returned a partial order without an error.
parts.modelAnswer: A cycle: no topological order exists, and the planner hid it.

parts.criteria: Fix the wrong edges so dependencies follow the data (reports before reports_cache; finance_close after ledger_load only), and make the planner raise on a cycle. Appending leftovers runs a cycle in some order that always violates an edge; stripping dependencies runs jobs before their inputs.

right.headline: Good: no order exists, so fix the graph
right.body: A topological order exists only for an acyclic graph. The cycle the new edges made kept three jobs from ever becoming ready; correcting the edges and making the planner refuse a cycle fixed this run and the next.

scoring.modelReasoning: The planner is Kahn's algorithm: it places a job once all its dependencies are placed. If a cycle exists, the jobs on it never reach in-degree 0, so no topological order exists; this planner returned the partial order as success. A depth-first search finds the back edge reports_cache -> reports, closing reports -> finance_close -> reports_cache -> reports. Yesterday's edges were backwards: reports_cache is built from reports, and finance_close needs only the ledger. Correct them, make the planner raise CycleError when jobs are left over, and check that all 12 are planned with every edge in order. Appending leftovers or stripping dependencies runs jobs before their inputs.
